---
title: "Downloading the demo data"
---

The demo databases let you explore real SpectroMesa results without running the
mass spectrometry pipelines yourself. They cover two experiments: an interferon
response in HepG2 cells, measured by both DIA and DDA, and an MTM1 experiment in
HeLa cells measured with TMT.

## 1. About the datasets

### 1.1. HepG2: interferon response measured by DIA and DDA LFQ

These data come from the study by Zou and colleagues comparing DDA and DIA
proteomics. The demo selection contains three control samples and three samples
treated with **100 ng/mL interferon α-2a for 12 hours**. Each acquisition mode has
its own database, so you can follow the same biological comparison using DIA or
DDA label-free results. [1](#ref-1)

The original data are available through iProX under
[IPX0013929001](https://www.iprox.cn/page/project.html?id=IPX0013929000).
DDA and DIA were acquired in separate batches; treat them as separate analyses
when working through the examples.

### 1.2. HeLa: MTM1 and TMT quantitation

These data come from Jang and colleagues' study of how endosomal lipid signaling
connects nutrient availability with organelle structure and mitochondrial
function. The demo uses the **fed-cell TMT10 plex**, acquired across **12
fractions**, from the deposited HeLa experiment. It includes control and MTM1
knockout samples, alongside siMTM1 samples and a pooled reference channel.
[2](#ref-2)

The original data are available through PRIDE under
[PXD033850](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/archive/projects/PXD033850). The full study
also includes starvation experiments; the demo selects the fed plex.

## 2. Processing with SpectroMesa

We reprocessed the selected raw data with the SpectroMesa versions below, then
assembled the results into DuckDB databases with
[ProteoVault](https://github.com/TheBoutrosLab/package-ProteoVault). These downloads
contain our SpectroMesa results, rather than the original authors' result tables.

| Demo dataset | Pipeline used |
| --- | --- |
| HepG2 DIA | [SpectroMesa-DIA v1.6.2](https://github.com/TheBoutrosLab/SpectroMesa-DIA/releases/tag/v1.6.2) |
| HepG2 DDA LFQ | [SpectroMesa-DDA v1.3.2](https://github.com/TheBoutrosLab/SpectroMesa-DDA/releases/tag/v1.3.2), with label-free quantitation |
| HeLa TMT | [SpectroMesa-DDA v1.3.2](https://github.com/TheBoutrosLab/SpectroMesa-DDA/releases/tag/v1.3.2), with TMT quantitation |

## 3. Download the databases

Choose the dataset you want to explore, or download all three. The databases are
hosted in the Boutros Lab public S3 bucket and total approximately **1.2 GB**.
Public downloads do not require an AWS account or credentials.

| Dataset | Database |
| --- | --- |
| HepG2 DIA | [hepg2_ifna-dia.proteovault.duckdb](https://boutroslab-public.s3.amazonaws.com/test-data/spectromesa/hepg2_ifna-dia.proteovault.duckdb) |
| HepG2 DDA LFQ | [hepg2_ifna-lfq.proteovault.duckdb](https://boutroslab-public.s3.amazonaws.com/test-data/spectromesa/hepg2_ifna-lfq.proteovault.duckdb) |
| HeLa TMT | [hela_mtm1-tmt.proteovault.duckdb](https://boutroslab-public.s3.amazonaws.com/test-data/spectromesa/hela_mtm1-tmt.proteovault.duckdb) |

Use the links above or run the R commands below. The code on this page is not
executed when the documentation is built.

### 3.1. Choose a download directory

Run the following in R from the directory where you want to work on the example
analyses. This creates a `demo-data` folder for the databases. You can replace
`"demo-data"` with another location if you prefer.

```{r download-directory, eval=FALSE}
data_dir <- "demo-data"
dir.create(data_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

base_url <- "https://boutroslab-public.s3.amazonaws.com/test-data/spectromesa"
files <- c(
    tmt = "hela_mtm1-tmt.proteovault.duckdb",
    dia = "hepg2_ifna-dia.proteovault.duckdb",
    lfq = "hepg2_ifna-lfq.proteovault.duckdb"
)

# Allow more time for these large downloads.
options(timeout = max(3600, getOption("timeout")))
```

### 3.2. Download a dataset

For the HepG2 DIA example, download the DIA database:

```{r download-one, eval=FALSE}
filename <- files[["dia"]]
download.file(
    url = paste(base_url, filename, sep = "/"),
    destfile = file.path(data_dir, filename),
    mode = "wb"
)
```

Use `files[["lfq"]]` for HepG2 DDA LFQ or `files[["tmt"]]` for HeLa TMT.
Each file is already a DuckDB database and does not need to be extracted.
Keep the filenames unchanged so you can reuse the paths in later examples.

To download all three instead, run:

```{r download-all, eval=FALSE}
for (filename in files) {
    download.file(
        url = paste(base_url, filename, sep = "/"),
        destfile = file.path(data_dir, filename),
        mode = "wb"
    )
}
```

::: {.alert .alert-info role="note"}
**Tip:** Download each database once, then reuse the saved copy in later sessions.
If a download is interrupted, rerun it and let it finish before opening the file.
:::

## 4. Open a downloaded database

For example, open the HepG2 DIA database and inspect its contents:

```{r open-demo, eval=FALSE}
library(ProteoVaultR)

vault <- open_vault(
    path = file.path(data_dir, files[["dia"]])
)
vault_info(vault)
close_vault(vault)
```

ProteoVaultR opens the database read-only. Close the connection when you have
finished working with it. Continue with [Exploring a database](exploring-a-database.html)
to learn how to inspect the experiment and retrieve results.

## 5. S3 locations

The original objects are:

```text
s3://boutroslab-public/test-data/spectromesa/hela_mtm1-tmt.proteovault.duckdb
s3://boutroslab-public/test-data/spectromesa/hepg2_ifna-dia.proteovault.duckdb
s3://boutroslab-public/test-data/spectromesa/hepg2_ifna-lfq.proteovault.duckdb
```
